thread:
marta: quick heads-up 00: opened RFC/PR that touches the glossary and several SDK examples. noticed product UI calls it "model version" but SDK examples (and some params) still say `model_revision`. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/492

docs-bot: auto-check -> link error in /sdk/js/README.md: line ~42 (404). please correct before merge.

laura: thanks for flagging. i'll take the glossary edit if we agree on the canonical term.

sahil: my vote: make user-facing docs say "model version". it's clearer in sales collateral too.

kevin: background: internal infra and telemetry use `model_revision`. SDKs historically mirrored that. changing the API field name is disruptive, but docs can and should prefer a friendly term.

marta: suggested approach (minimal user disruption):
1) docs: present "model version" as the canonical user term; explicitly note "internally called `model_revision`" and link to a short migration note.
2) SDKs: implement backwards-compatible aliases so both names work; emit deprecation warnings when the old name is used.
3) examples: update all code snippets to show the preferred param name first, then show the legacy form under "compatibility".
4) fix the broken js README link.

kevin: agreed. i'll open a small SDK change that accepts both `model_revision` and `model_version` / camelCase modelVersion in JS, with a unit test asserting they behave identically. i'll also add a console.warn in JS and DeprecationWarning in Python when the legacy name is used.

kevin: snippet i'll add to the docs (different form):
```python
# preferred user-facing example
resp = client.generate(model_version="redwood-3", prompt="Hey")
# legacy form still accepted (emits DeprecationWarning)
resp2 = client.generate(model_revision="redwood-3", prompt="Hey")
assert resp.tokens == resp2.tokens
```

```js
// preferred
const r = await client.generate({ modelVersion: 'redwood-3', prompt: 'Hey' })
// legacy
const r2 = await client.generate({ modelRevision: 'redwood-3', prompt: 'Hey' }) // logs warning
```

laura: for the glossary entry i suggest a single-sentence definition plus a pointer to the migration note: "model version: the user-facing name for a specific model snapshot used for inference. Historically referenced as `model_revision` in internal APIs; see migration notes for SDK guidance."

sahil: can we also add a one-liner for the release notes so GTM knows to surface the wording change? they often copy docs material into decks.

marta: yes i'll add a short blurb to the release notes and ping growth/sales.

docs-bot: reminder: SDK PRs require a CHANGELOG entry and passing linter + tests.

laura: i'll update glossary.md and add a small "migration" section in /docs/guides explaining mapping and linking to SDK examples. i'll also fix the broken link in the JS README while i'm at it.

kevin: ETA: i'll open the SDK alias PR by EOD tomorrow with tests. i'll include a tiny note in the API reference that server responses still include `model_revision` but that docs refer to it as "model version".

marta: action items:
- laura: update glossary + migration section + fix js readme link (assigned)
- kevin: SDK alias PR + tests + changelog entry (in progress)
- marta: add release-note blurb + ping growth (todo)
- sahil: review release-note wording (todo)

sahil: thanks team. if the SDK changes end up touching telemetry tags, please let platform/infra know so they don't misinterpret metrics.

kevin: good point00: i'll coordinate with infra and include a unit test that asserts the telemetry tag name remains stable.

marta: perfect. i'll post PR numbers here once they exist. thanks everyone :rocket:
